title: At-Tin: the fig and the olive
hook: by the fig, the olive, Sinai and the safe city, the human was made in the best stature (Surah 95)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Al-'Alaq, and the man who tried to stop a servant from praying. Your line was bow and draw near.

A companion of the Prophet named al-Bara' remembered one night on a journey. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ led the evening prayer and recited a short surah that starts with fruit: by the fig and the olive. Al-Bara' said, and it's recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari, that he had never heard anyone with a more beautiful voice or recitation. Of all the things he might have remembered from his time with the Prophet, he remembered a voice, at night, reciting about figs.
screen: `A NIGHT ON A JOURNEY.` → `BY THE FIG AND THE OLIVE.` → `THE MOST BEAUTIFUL VOICE.`

segments.voice: Surah ninety-five opens with four oaths, in Pickthall's translation: By the fig and the olive, By Mount Sinai, And by this land made safe. Why fig and olive? Commentators give two answers, and hold both. The fruits themselves, gifts of the earth, sweet and nourishing. And the places they grow: some commentators link the fig and olive to the lands around Jerusalem, home to earlier prophets. Mount Sinai is where Musa received revelation, and this land made safe is Mecca, where the Prophet was. So some scholars read the oaths as a map of revelation: the lands of the prophets, Musa's mountain, Muhammad's city. Then the point of all four oaths: Surely We created man of the best stature. Ahsan taqwim: the finest form, the best proportion, body and mind and soul. That's the Qur'an's starting point about human beings: made well, beautifully, on purpose. Then a hard line: then We reduced him to the lowest of the low. Commentators read it several ways: old age and frailty, or the fall that comes when a person turns away. Except, it says, those who believe and do good. They have a reward that never ends. So the surah holds both: made in the best form, and able to fall far from it. The dignity is the beginning, not something you have to earn. What you do with it is the story.
screen: `FIG, OLIVE, SINAI, THE SAFE LAND.` · `A MAP OF REVELATION.` · `AHSAN TAQWIM — THE BEST STATURE.` · `THE LOWEST OF THE LOW, EXCEPT —` · then, large: `MADE IN THE BEST FORM.`

segments.voice: Hold a fig or an olive, or any fruit, and look at it closely, the color, the skin, how it's put together; then eat it slowly, and if you pray, say bismillah first and alhamdulillah after. If you don't have one, look at your own hand the same way: the joints, the lines, how it moves.
At-Tin. The fig, the first oath of Surah ninety-five, which says the human was made in the best stature. Today's word.
Your line: made in the best form. That goes for the face in the mirror, and for every other face too. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: At-Tin is recited in the prayers, and the Prophet recited it in the evening prayer while traveling; its verse on the best stature is often quoted in teaching about human dignity.

chat.says: What does the surah of the fig and the olive say about people?
options: That we were made in the best form, though we can fall far from it.
That we start out low and have to earn our dignity over a lifetime.
That people are bad at heart, and nothing they do can change that.
chat.meaning: Verse four: We created man of the best stature. The dignity is the beginning; what you do with it is the story.

Musa.meaning: the prophet Moses, who received revelation at Sinai

Ahsan taqwim.meaning: the finest form, the best proportion

bismillah.meaning: in the name of God, said before beginning

alhamdulillah.meaning: praise be to God, said in thanks

notes: Please confirm the exact Pickthall wording of 95:1–4.

The reading of the oaths as places (Holy Land, Sinai, Mecca) is one common view (Ibn Kathir); others take the fig and olive literally or link them to other places. The script says 'many commentators'.
'The dignity comes first' is the writer's framing of 95:4; confirm it fits.
